summary: Collects the ASN.1 definitions of the component matching rules for LDAP and X.500 directories into one properly identified ASN.1 module. That lets other specifications import those definitions into their own ASN.1 modules. It updates the earlier rules in RFC 3687 in form rather than adding new behavior.

eli5.summary: A rulebook was scattered over many pages. This puts the rules together in one clearly labeled chapter so other books can point right to it.

subtitle: A tidy ASN.1 module that gathers the LDAP and X.500 component matching rules in one place others can import.

tldr.problem: RFC 3687 defines component matching rules for LDAP and X.500 directories, but its ASN.1 definitions were not in a module that other specifications could reference.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3727 collects those ASN.1 definitions into one identified module, ComponentMatching, without changing them.
tldr.outcome: Other specifications can now import the component matching definitions from within their own ASN.1 modules.

today: RFC 3727 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It updates RFC 3687 by supplying the module.

sections.title: Why a Separate Module
sections.content:
Data held in an attribute of an LDAP or X.500 directory is described by the attribute's syntax, which can be simple (text, integer, boolean) or complex. RFC 3687 defines a generic way to match user-selected components inside an attribute value of any syntax.

RFC 3727 updates RFC 3687 by collecting its ASN.1 definitions into an appropriately identified module, so that other specifications can reference them from their own ASN.1 modules. It adds no new behavior.
sections.eli5: A rulebook was spread over many pages. This puts all the rules in one labeled chapter so other books can point at it.

sections.title: The ComponentMatching Module
sections.content:
The module is named ComponentMatching and uses EXPLICIT TAGS and EXTENSIBILITY IMPLIED. It imports MATCHING-RULE and RelativeDistinguishedName from the InformationFramework module defined in X.501.

It defines a ComponentAssertion (an optional component reference, a useDefaultValues flag that defaults to TRUE, a matching rule and an assertion value) and a ComponentFilter, which is either one assertion or an and, or or not combination of filters.

It also defines the matching rules componentFilterMatch, allComponentsMatch and directoryComponentsMatch, plus two additional useful rules, rdnMatch and presentMatch.
sections.eli5: The module is a list of building blocks for asking questions about parts of a record, such as 'this part equals that' or 'not this and that'.

sections.title: Object Identifiers
sections.content: Each matching rule carries an object identifier. These were assigned by Adacel Technologies, under an arc assigned to Adacel by Standards Australia, for specifying the component matching rules.
sections.eli5: Every rule gets its own unique ID number, like a library call number, so nobody mixes them up.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document collects the ASN.1 definitions together but does not modify them in any way. For the security considerations of using the component matching rules, the RFC points to RFC 3687.
sections.eli5: Nothing was changed, only moved, so the safety advice is still in the original book.
